newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end lower but remain in recent range.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end lower but remain in recent range.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed weaker as the market maintained its recent sideways to lower trading pattern amid an ongoing negative fundamental picture.
Florida remains on track to produce a record crop in 1996/97, while high retail prices continue to squeeze U.S. demand for juice.

The market tried to rally on early trade buying, which carried the spot July contract to a high of 77.50 cents, just over the nine-day moving average of 77.30 cents. Failing to maintain gains, prices drifted for most of the day until speculative selling ahead of the close pressured the market to the day's lows.
Spot July orange juice settled 0.95 cent weaker at 75.90 cents per lb, after ranging from 77.50 to 75.50 cents. The rest of the board closed 0.75 to 2.35 weaker.
Meantime, open interest continues to surge. As of Tuesday, open interest stood at 34,972 lots, up 575 lots.
"We have a stronger negative market than we think," a broker said.
An estimated 2,800 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Monday's official 2,232 lots.
